title: Revenant
tagline: Prove your database backups actually recover
description: Connects to PostgreSQL (local or AWS RDS), runs validation checks from revenant.yaml, measures recovery time, writes reports, and tears down test sandboxes. Language-agnostic — your app can be Node, Python, Go, or anything.

blocks.title: Problem
blocks.text: Backups that never get restored are wishful thinking. Revenant proves restores work — not just that backup jobs completed.

items: Download binary from GitHub Releases (Linux, Mac, Windows)
Build from source: go build for contributors

blocks.code:
- uses: 277pawan/revenant-action@v1.0.3
  with:
    version: v0.1.1
    config: revenant.yaml
  env:
    DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.DATABASE_URL }}

export DATABASE_URL='postgres://user:pass@localhost:5432/mydb?sslmode=disable'
revenant init --plan my-app --force
revenant verify

blocks.title: Expected output
blocks.text: Schema checks, row counts, foreign keys pass → Restore Validation: PASS → Wrote report.json and report.md

rows: Run checks; optional AWS snapshot restore

blocks.code:
checks:
  - type: connect
  - type: schema
    expect_tables: [customers, orders]
  - type: row_count
    table: orders
    min: 1
  - type: foreign_key
    table: orders
    references: customers
  - type: golden_query
    query: "SELECT count(*) FROM orders"
    expect_min: 1
  - type: freshness
    table: orders
    column: created_at
    max_age: 24h

blocks.text: Optional recovery.engine: aws-rds restores latest snapshot to a temporary sandbox, runs checks, destroys sandbox. Use revenant reap in CI with if: always() as a safety net.
